findings.title: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process never matches spawn processes, so hung flusher processes are never killed
findings.body: Flusher processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process`, where `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context('spawn')`, so they are instances of `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. On Linux, `multiprocessing.Process` resolves to the default (fork) context's `ForkProcess` class — a sibling of `SpawnProcess`, not a parent — so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is always False and `process.kill()` is never executed. Previously `kill()` was called unconditionally (guarded only by try/except ValueError), so this is a regression. Consequence: when a flusher process hangs (still alive but not updating `healthy_since`), the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` starts a new process for those shards without killing the old one, leaving two processes flushing the same shards concurrently — producing duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic and racing on `done_flush_segments`. The same incorrect guard at line 346 in `join()` means `process.terminate()` is also silently skipped for spawn processes, so the shutdown fallback never force-terminates them. Use `multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess` (or `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`) for the isinstance check instead.

findings.title: The added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched, leaving the race it was meant to fix
findings.body: In `test_basic`, `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` is applied at the top of the test, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` (with the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') resolves to the patched no-op and does not actually wait. The race it was intended to close is still present: `step.join()` sets `stopped.value = True` immediately, so if the flusher thread has not run a loop iteration between `fac._flusher.current_drift.value = 9000` and `join()`, it exits without flushing and `(msg,) = messages` fails. The test will be flaky under thread scheduling jitter. Either capture the real `time.sleep` before monkeypatching and call that, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a real deadline.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is introduced in this PR but never called anywhere — the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. Worse, if it ever were used naively it would restart the entire process for a shard without updating `self.processes` consistently with the caller. It should be removed to avoid confusion about the restart API.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag keys: 'shard' vs 'shards'
findings.body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` timer and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` timing are tagged with key `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with key `shards` (and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` uses `shard`). Because the tag keys differ, the wait_produce metric cannot be grouped or filtered alongside the other flusher metrics in dashboards/monitors. Pick one tag key and use it consistently.
